previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple myeloma, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, and chronic hemolytic anemia, was admitted with fever, confusion, and abdominal distension following an IVIG infusion. He had recently restarted oral vancomycin for a recurrent C. difficile infection. Workup revealed no growth in blood or urine cultures, a normal head CT and chest imaging, but a CT abdomen/pelvis showed rectal wall thickening consistent with proctitis. His symptoms were attributed to C. difficile colitis, and he was transitioned to fidaxomicin. Encephalopathy resolved within 48 hours, and he remained afebrile by discharge. He developed transient preseptal edema, ruled out for orbital cellulitis, likely due to fluid shifts. His anemia and thrombocytopenia were managed supportively, with aspirin held. He completed dialysis, remained on chemotherapy, and was discharged to extended care rehab to finish treatment and continue recovery.
